title: Draft save returns ok:true when the 500/vacancy cap silently drops the write
detail: Cap rejection makes INSERT...SELECT yield zero rows, so upsert returns Ok with 0 rows; handler matches Ok(_) and answers ok:true. A new applicant's answers are not saved while the UI claims they are. On the continue-link path the same no-op leads to claim finding no row, sent:false, and the UI still reading "Link sent".
recommended_fix: Distinguish zero-row Ok for a non-existent pair (cap hit) from the deliberate tombstone/submitted no-op; on cap rejection return a non-ok JSON so the client stops promising saves.

title: 500/vacancy cap counts tombstoned and submitted rows that persist until vacancy close
evidence:
OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
---
-- A successful final POST makes the application row the system of record:
-- empty the draft's PII payload, kill the continue token, and stamp the
-- resume→submit metric. The row itself stays (email + timestamps only)
-- until the retention sweep removes it at vacancy close.
---
-- hard delete. Fields/token/link-stamps are wiped and erased_at set; the
-- (vacancy, email) key is kept as a suppression record until the retention
-- sweep removes it at vacancy close
detail: Strip-on-submit and erasure deliberately keep their rows until vacancy close, and the cap subquery has no submitted_at/erased_at filter. Every submission permanently consumes draft-cap headroom, so a high-traffic vacancy exhausts the 500 on dead rows and starts rejecting live drafts.
recommended_fix: Add AND d.submitted_at IS NULL AND d.erased_at IS NULL to the count subquery so the cap bounds live drafts; dead rows are not attacker-scalable (submit/erasure are gated).

title: resumed_at stamping is asymmetric on empty fields; "Same re-engagement stamp" comment is false
detail: With an empty fields map, the save path early-returns before the resume_token stamp, but the continue-link path stamps resumed_at anyway (upsert skipped, stamp still runs). The comment claiming parity with the plain save path is wrong for exactly this case; the re-engagement metric diverges between endpoints.
recommended_fix: Gate the continue-link stamp the same way (only when an actual upsert ran), or fix the comment and pin the intended asymmetry.

title: Resume page restores values to every section except review_consent, but filter_fields still saves that section's non-consent fields
evidence:
form_sections.view_section_about_you(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_your_situation(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_work_income(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_references(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_guarantor(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_tell_us_more(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_documents(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_review_consent(errors: []),
---
    !string.starts_with(key, "_")
    && key != "gdpr_consent"
    && !is_file_slot_key(key)
detail: filter_fields excludes only _-prefixed internals, gdpr_consent, and file slots, so any other review_consent-section input (e.g. the §5.4 attestation radios evidenced by attestation_choice_error in form_copy) is persisted into the draft — yet view_resume_page passes no values to that section, so those saved values are never restored.
recommended_fix: Either exclude the consent-section non-consent fields in filter_fields (like gdpr_consent) or pass values to view_section_review_consent on the resume page; don't round-trip dead data.
